decisive_items: a dense acute neutrophilic infiltrate extending into adipose tissue and septa
Direct immunofluorescence of the lesion was negative
response.rationale: Skin biopsy showing neutrophilic panniculitis with negative DIF is specific and directly supports R3. R1 lacks biopsy confirmation and is contradicted by negative DIF; other candidates are historical or non-specific.

rejected.why: No evidence of autoimmune hepatitis flare; biopsy and symptoms point to skin/adipose inflammation.
Azathioprine-induced vasculitis is speculative; negative DIF and neutrophilic panniculitis pattern argue against vasculitis.
GI symptoms are present but biopsy findings are not explained by ulcerative colitis flare.
Sickle cell crisis does not explain the specific neutrophilic panniculitis biopsy.
Autoimmune vasculitis is possible but lacks biopsy support; negative DIF and neutrophilic panniculitis favor R3.
